question.problem: In what direction does the function $g(x,y,z)={e}^{xy}+3{z}^{2}y$ increase most rapidly at the point $(2,2,-1)?$
question.worked_solution:
At a given point, a function $g(x,y,z)$ increases most rapidly in the direction of its gradient at that point.

So, we compute $∇g(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at the point $(2,2,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{xy}+3{z}^{2}y),\,\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{xy}+3{z}^{2}y),\,\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{xy}+3{z}^{2}y)⟩ \\  & =⟨y{e}^{xy},\,x{e}^{xy}+3{z}^{2},\,6yz⟩ \\ ∇g(2,2,-1) & =⟨2\cdot {e}^{2\cdot 2},\,2\cdot {e}^{2\cdot 2}+3(-1)^{2},\,6\cdot 2\cdot (-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{4},\,2{e}^{4}+3,\,-12⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the function increases most rapidly in the direction of $⟨2{e}^{4},\,2{e}^{4}+3,\,-12⟩.$
